claim.statement: Trident Techlabs reports deliberate investment in its semiconductor design subsidiary and international operations together with recruitment of engineering and technical talent to build execution capacity for an expanding pipeline.

review.note: Operational capability investment and hiring support execution headroom; this is not labelled manufacturing capacity.

claim.statement: Trident Techlabs has a wholly owned UAE subsidiary and is investing in international operations to broaden its addressable market.

review.note: Existing UAE subsidiary and current international investment make this concrete geography optionality.

source_locator.note: Power solutions product roadmap in earnings call

claim.statement: Management says its indigenous phase-identification product design is complete, the product is under testing with about 90% results proven, and it intends to take the product to market in the upcoming months.

review.note: Specific product has completed design and is under testing; launch is prospective, not assumed completed.

claim.statement: Management states that order-in-hand is approximately INR 35 crore, including items that will be billed over future periods such as AMC, services and facility-management components.

review.note: Explicit current order-in-hand disclosure; not extrapolated to future order wins.

source_locator.note: Opening management guidance plus later Q&A qualification

claim.statement: Management guides to approximately 30% CAGR in consolidated revenue, EBITDA and PAT over the next three years; later in the same call the CEO explicitly characterises the 30% figure as guidance rather than a firm commitment.

review.note: Stored as measurable management guidance for prospective delivery tracking. The same-call qualification is preserved and no Management Execution score is created now.

explicit_rejections.reason: The press release uses 'execution capacity' for human/operational capability, not disclosed manufacturing capacity. No CAPACITY claim is created.
Long OEM relationships and management's own use of the word 'moat' are useful context but do not yet independently satisfy the frozen moat evidence categories strongly enough for a score.
